vision_boundary_flip — DRIVE pegfail op

• Data kinds: table × signal × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.vision_boundary_flip(kp, eps_true, sigma: 'float', n: 'int' = 2000, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import pegfail; pegfail.vision_boundary_flip(kp, eps_true, sigma: 'float', n: 'int' = 2000, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("vision_boundary_flip"))

Usage

"Where does it break": when measurement noise with standard deviation σ is added to the true offset ε, counts at each ε the probability that the offset field (small/large, boundary W + c_r) is flipped relative to the truth (numpy only). Also returns how many σ the point lies from the boundary (z) and the theoretical value Φ(−|z|) (a gate that matches when the noise is Gaussian).

> The detailed description below is the original text — the summary and the headings are translated.

返り: eps(m)、flip_rate、z = (|ε| − eps_max)/σ、flip_theory = Φ(−|z|)、eps_max。Raises ValueError: σ ≤ 0。
